`smysl fmt` now skips its verification reparse when the canonical form is byte-identical to the input. The `smysl-core` tests pass. In `cargo test -q -p smysl --tests --no-fail-fast`, one target fails, `doc_output`, and it is unrelated to this change.

**The change** is in `cmd_fmt` in `src/main.rs`. The round-trip check now runs only when `formatted != src`. For an already-formatted file, the second parse would read the same bytes as the first and can only return the same records. The check still runs on any file `fmt` actually rewrites. Output and exit codes are unchanged.

**The `doc_output` failure** is in `the_manual_still_describes_this_binary`. It expects `smysl attest --what gist-coverage` to print `provider unreachable`, but in this environment the provider answered. I stashed my changes and ran it on the clean tree, and it fails there in the same way.

I also added an assertion to the existing check-versus-canonical test in `tests/cmd_fmt.rs`. It confirms a canonical file still prints itself unchanged and reports no identity drift. The skip changes nothing observable, so no test can detect it directly.

I added a `CHANGELOG.md` entry under 1.4.0. Nothing is committed.
